message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this situation.

Position: $1,000 USDC in Morpho MetaMorpho vault "Steakhouse USDC" on Ethereum. No debt. Vault lends against BTC/ETH blue-chip collateral.

Observations:
1. O01: Normal vault state at 00:00 UTC. Total assets 125.61M, share price stable (+0.002%). Utilization ~90% across markets, decent liquidity. All normal.
2. O02: Routine reallocation tx by allocator — normal vault management activity, repeats every ~30 min. Normal.
3. O03: Vault accepted pending caps for NEW markets (wstETH/USDC, cbBTC/USDC, WBTC/USDC) with large caps, added to withdraw queue. Collateral types unchanged (BTC/ETH blue chips). Submitted 8 days earlier — normal governance timelock process.

Is there anything risky here? The new markets have the same collateral types (blue chips). Caps acceptance is a routine governance action. Adding to withdraw queue is standard. No exploit, no oracle issue, no depeg, no pause, no liquidity crisis. Utilization at 90% is somewhat high but liquidity is ample ($15M+, $25M+ etc.) relative to user's $1,000 position.

The new markets could theoretically be riskier versions (different LLTV, oracle), but the observation says collateral types unchanged. Nothing indicates an incident. This is noise/routine operations.

Risk: low. Action: hold.

Reasons: vault operating normally, share price stable, routine allocator reallocations, routine cap acceptance for new markets with same blue-chip collateral, ample liquidity vs position size.

Source ids: O01, O02, O03 — maybe all three since they collectively support "normal operations". Or just O01 and O03. I'll include all three as they drove the assessment.
